I believe that I understood the Prosecutor to say that there would be a meeting with Mr. Kostic. Perhaps you can discuss that issue and inform us of the results of your discussion. Since this is something which is not going to happen right now, and we hope that it won't ever happen, from the point of view of the practicality of the decision, you already have it in oral form which allows you to work in order to provide the documents. You're going to meet with Mr. Kostic and you will give to us the results, even through Mr. Olivier Fourmy, and you could sign the same piece of paper, after which, in the written decision, we will consider what you've said to us. Do you all agree? Mr. Kostic, is that agreeable to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOSTIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those were the questions that you wanted to raise. I don't know whether Mr. Kostic wants to raise anything else that was not on the agenda. Are there any points that we have not yet dealt with?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOSTIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the only thing that I want to go back to, and only very briefly, because I think the Prosecutor might have misunderstood me, has to do with the issue of whether or not Mr. Galic would testify and when. I think he was under the impression that I may choose to have Mr. Galic -- perhaps, as one of the options -- to have him testify in the beginning or right after the opening statements. I think that he misunderstood me, maybe. What I said is he would either testify at the beginning of the Defence case or at the end of the Defence case, not before the Prosecution case. So I just wanted to clarify that for the Prosecutor because I thought maybe he misunderstood me. Other than that, Your Honour, I have no other questions or requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that, but I thought he might change his opinion during the trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. It's clear now, that is, Mr. Kostic's position is clear. But of course Mr. Kostic can change his mind. We've got a lot of time yet before the trial begins, and this is something that Mr. Kostic will discuss with General Galic. Let me now turn to the last point on the agenda, after a very long day. I turn to General Galic. Would you rise, please, General Galic

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I give you the opportunity to speak to us about your detention conditions and your medical condition.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I wish to thank you for having given me some time today as well to say a few words. First of all, the condition of my health is somewhat better than it was before. My leg is my greatest problem, the one that was hurt during my arrest. I'm working with a physical therapist now, and whether we will succeed or not, that is to be seen. As for the rest of my health problems, they are getting better, more or less. As far as the detention conditions are concerned, they are quite fair. I think that the transfer to this other building created a few problems, but that's being worked out with the management. However, there is another problem that should be resolved as quickly as possible. We haven't got a single TV programme in our language, and you know what the situation is like. So I would appreciate it very much if you could do something about this. Mr. McFadden, the warden, has made every effort conceivable. But this is one of the things that I wished to draw your attention to. As for the rest, in my opinion and judging by everything I can see, I think that everything seems to be all right, and I thank you. However, with your permission, I would just like to raise another question that has been tormenting me, so to speak, and you have not raised it. Thank you. I'm a bit concerned about this treatment of my Defence, I mean, the status of Mr. Kostic. It's been four months now. All of this is provisional; all of this is temporary. He is on his own; he does not have a team. I've been retired since 1994, so that is my situation, I'm a retiree. And if he is my only defence counsel, I must say that this has led me to think about certain things that I would not like to dwell on for very long here today. That is this additional point that I wish to make which causes great concern to me. After all, it worries me more than anything else. Because what is the point of all of this trial if I don't have a Defence? Then I can just remain silent if I don't have a proper Defence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar please take note of these comments and transmit them to Madam Registrar. I do hope that your leg continues to heal. Very well. We have now reached the end of the Status Conference, because I think we have really reached the beginning of the work. I thank everybody, specifically the interpreters. As I said, we worked together all day long, and we'll be seeing one another again tomorrow. If somebody says that we don't work, I think we can show that we do. I wish the parties success in their work, and if there are any questions, they should be raised, and you can always contact me or Mr. Fourmy for any questions that you might have. The Pre-Trial Judge may even have meetings outside of this calendar, and even in his own office. So he remains available, but things have to be organised, because I spend more time in court than, of course, I do in my office, and it would be difficult for us to meet. Continue your work, and I wish you all a good evening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: adjourned at 6.10 p.m.
